### client-vpn-active-directory-via-directory-service-ad-connector

**Claim.** Client VPN integrates with Directory Service to authenticate clients against existing Active Directory groups, in AWS or on premises. For an on-premises Active Directory without an existing AWS Managed Microsoft AD, you must configure an AD Connector.

**Write it as.** `Active Directory support by integrating with Directory Service` · `configure an Active Directory Connector (AD Connector)`

**Scope.** Client VPN Active Directory authentication.

> "Client VPN provides Active Directory support by integrating with Directory Service. With Active Directory authentication, clients are authenticated against existing Active Directory groups. Using Directory Service, Client VPN can connect to existing Active Directories provisioned in AWS or in your on-premises network. This allows you to use your existing client authentication infrastructure. If you are using an on-premises Active Directory and you do not have an existing AWS Managed Microsoft AD, you must configure an Active Directory Connector (AD Connector)."
> — [Active Directory authentication in Client VPN](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/clientvpn-admin/ad.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-14.

**Changed.** 2025-03-18: was 10 routes per association.

### client-vpn-split-tunnel-benefit-lower-data-transfer-cost

**Claim.** Split-tunnel lets only AWS-destined traffic use the VPN tunnel, and it reduces the volume of outgoing traffic from AWS, which reduces the data transfer cost.

**Write it as.** `reducing the data transfer cost` · `AWS destined traffic traverse the VPN tunnel`

**Scope.** Client VPN split-tunnel.

> "You can optimize the routing of traffic from clients by having only the AWS destined traffic traverse the VPN tunnel."
> — [Split-tunnel on AWS Client VPN endpoints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/clientvpn-admin/split-tunnel-vpn.html)

> "You can reduce the volume of outgoing traffic from AWS, therefore reducing the data transfer cost."
> — [Split-tunnel on AWS Client VPN endpoints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/clientvpn-admin/split-tunnel-vpn.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-14.

### client-vpn-split-tunnel-default-off-all-traffic-through-tunnel

**Claim.** By default all traffic from Client VPN clients is routed over the VPN tunnel. With split-tunnel turned on, only traffic destined for a network that matches a route in the endpoint route table goes over the tunnel.

**Write it as.** `all traffic from clients is routed` · `only traffic with a destination to the network`

**Scope.** Client VPN endpoint; default; adjustable; enable split-tunnel on the endpoint.

> "By default, when you have a Client VPN endpoint, all traffic from clients is routed over the Client VPN tunnel. When you enable split-tunnel on the Client VPN endpoint, we push the routes on the Client VPN endpoint route table to the device that is connected to the Client VPN endpoint. This ensures that only traffic with a destination to the network matching a route from the Client VPN endpoint route table is routed over the Client VPN tunnel."
> — [Split-tunnel on AWS Client VPN endpoints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/clientvpn-admin/split-tunnel-vpn.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-14.
